scenes.title: Counter-Syllogism and Objection
scenes.summary: One solves an argument by a counter-syllogism or by an objection; objections come from the thing itself, from the like, from the opposite, or from previous judgments, as Pittacus' law answers the plea for the drunk.

scenes.title: Solving the Four Kinds of Enthymeme
scenes.summary: Enthymemes come from probabilities, examples, tekmēria and signs. Probabilities can always be met by an objection, though the judge should judge from probabilities too; signs and examples can be solved, tekmēria only by denying the fact.
